# Test fixtures

What each file here is, where it came from, and what a test may rely on it for.

| File                             | Harness       | Captured or hand-built                                                                          | What it proves                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------------------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `claude-code.stream.jsonl`       | `claude-code` | Captured from the real CLI, ids and paths scrubbed.                                             | The adapter reads a successful run: final text, a `Skill` call, tokens, cost, and the plugins of the init event. Its transcript proves `assistantText` and `toolOutputs`: a `user` event's `tool_result` joins the `Skill` call by id. |
| `claude-code-tools.stream.jsonl` | `claude-code` | Captured from the real CLI, ids and paths scrubbed.                                             | Each native tool name maps to its neutral kind. Every `message.id` is scrubbed to one value, so it proves nothing about turns.                                                                                                         |
| `claude-code-turns.stream.jsonl` | `claude-code` | Hand-built from the documented event shape, with distinct `message.id` and `tool_use.id`.       | Tool calls of one `message.id` share a turn, also when split over events, and each new id is the next turn. A capture replaces it.                                                                                                     |
| `codex.stream.jsonl`             | `codex`       | Captured from the real CLI, driven by a scripted local model endpoint.                          | The adapter reads a successful run and its tool items. Its transcript proves `assistantText` (`agent_message`), `toolOutputs` (`command_execution` `aggregated_output`) and the session id of `thread.started`.                        |
| `codex-error.stream.jsonl`       | `codex`       | Captured from the real CLI, driven by a scripted local model endpoint.                          | A failed run is reported as an error.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `cursor.stream.jsonl`            | `cursor`      | The example sequence of Cursor's output-format documentation; no authenticated CLI was at hand. | The adapter reads the documented shape. Nothing here was seen from a real run. Its transcript is read from this shape (`assistant` text, `tool_call` `started` and `completed`); cursor declares no transcript capability.             |
| `opencode.stream.jsonl`          | `opencode`    | Captured from the real CLI, driven by a scripted local model endpoint.                          | The adapter reads a successful run. Its transcript proves `assistantText` (`text`), `toolOutputs` (`tool_use` `state.output`) and `toolDurations` (`state.time`).                                                                      |
| `opencode-error.stream.jsonl`    | `opencode`    | Captured from the real CLI, driven by a scripted local model endpoint.                          | A failed run is reported as an error.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `pi.stream.jsonl`                | `pi`          | Captured from the real CLI, driven by a scripted local model endpoint.                          | The adapter reads a successful run and its tool calls. Its transcript proves `assistantText` (`turn_end` text), `toolOutputs` (`tool_execution_end`) and the session id of the `session` event.                                        |
| `pi-error.stream.jsonl`          | `pi`          | Captured from the real CLI, driven by a scripted local model endpoint.                          | A failed run is reported as an error.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `fake-harness.mjs`               | `claude-code` | Hand-built stand-in executable.                                                                 | A whole run with no model: scripted transcripts, a judge, plugin behaviours. It speaks Pi's stream when started with `--mode json`.                                                                                                    |
| `garbled-harness.mjs`            | `codex`       | Hand-built stand-in executable.                                                                 | A harness whose probe output cannot be read.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `logged-out-harness.mjs`         | `pi`          | Hand-built stand-in executable.                                                                 | A harness that is not logged in, for the probe.                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `slow-harness.mjs`               | `claude-code` | Hand-built stand-in executable.                                                                 | A harness that outlasts its timeout.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

## Streams written inside tests

`src/adapters-transcript.test.ts` also builds short streams by hand for the edges that no fixture has: an error result, a result that is a list of blocks, a tool with no output yet, a result with no call. Each is written from the event shape that the adapter already reads (`claude-code`, `codex`, `opencode` and `pi`) or from the CLI's documentation (`cursor`). They prove how a parser handles that shape. A capability is declared only for the captured fixtures above.
